proposed_widenings.name: subclass_grant
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature's entire mechanic is a character-build branching point: at level 3 the player chooses a subclass and gains its features for the rest of their career. This is not an activation (no cost, no resource, no reset cadence, no effect). No existing ClassFeatureMechanics family can encode a build-time subclass selection. ClassFeatureActivationMechanics requires activationCost + resource + resetCadence + effect, none of which are applicable. ClassFeatureEffect only covers GrantExtraActionEffect and HealHpEffect — neither represents 'choose a specialization path'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice. The Champion subclass is detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Fighter levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Fighter level or lower.

notes: This is a character-progression gate, not a runtime mechanic. The feature has no activation cost, no resource pool, no reset cadence, and no discrete effect atom — it is purely a build-time branching instruction ('pick a subclass'). The same structural gap applies to all *_subclass_l3 features across every class (barbarian, bard, cleric, druid, monk, paladin, ranger, rogue, sorcerer, warlock, wizard). A new ClassFeatureMechanics family ('subclass_grant' or similar) is needed to model this pattern. Forcing it into ClassFeatureActivationMechanics with a fake effect would produce a false trace.
